title: Transportation Inspectors
description: Inspect equipment or goods in connection with the safe transport of cargo or people. Includes rail transportation inspectors, such as freight inspectors, rail inspectors, and other inspectors of transportation vehicles not elsewhere classified.

tasks.text: Inspect shipments to ensure that freight is securely braced and blocked.
Observe loading of freight to ensure that crews comply with procedures.
Inspect loaded cargo, cargo lashed to decks or in storage facilities, and cargo handling devices to determine compliance with health and safety regulations and need for maintenance.

clusters.label: Estimating the Quantifiable Characteristics of Products, Events, or Information

tasks.text: Measure heights and widths of loads to ensure they will pass over bridges or through tunnels on scheduled routes.
Read draft markings to determine depths of vessels in water.
Calculate gross and net tonnage, hold capacities, volumes of stored fuel and water, cargo weights, and vessel stability factors, using mathematical formulas.
Measure vessels' holds and depths of fuel and water in tanks, using sounding lines and tape measures.
Prepare and submit reports after completion of freight shipments.
Record details about freight conditions, handling of freight, and any problems encountered.
Check temperatures and humidities of shipping and storage areas to ensure that they are at appropriate levels to protect cargo.
Visually inspect cargo for damage upon arrival or discharge.

clusters.label: Interpreting the Meaning of Information for Others

tasks.text: Advise crews in techniques of stowing dangerous and heavy cargo.
Post warning signs on vehicles containing explosives or flammable or radioactive materials.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Recommend remedial procedures to correct any violations found during inspections.
Notify workers of any special treatment required for shipments.
Direct crews to reload freight or to insert additional bracing or packing as necessary.
Determine cargo transportation capabilities by reading documents that set forth cargo loading and securing procedures, capacities, and stability factors.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Document management software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or search documents or files from other software or from paper copies. Examples: Adobe Acrobat.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Google Android.
